column8: Mon 16 Nov: 3a or 3e map, pattern 1: insurers break most often by setting aside too little (37.2% of property/casualty cases); property/casualty only, pair with row 3 for life.
Mon 16 Nov: store; the rest of Best's list from a search extract of the IAIR reprint (S 3); investment losses barely register for property/casualty.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a support for pattern 1 in both segments to 2009; the life share is printed without labels, so never quote a life percentage.
Mon 16 Nov: store; guards 'commonest cause' with its field and dates (life/health since 2000 has no single leader).
Mon 16 Nov: store; the EU's own census puts underpricing first; 20 firms over six years.
Mon 16 Nov: store; 'no management layer' is untrue (BlackRock advises the funds; the 2031 move is a decision): say no one makes investment decisions on the reserve after January 2028.
Mon 16 Nov: 2.3 or 3e; 74.5% and 56.4% match NUMBERS 5, but never 'the one correlated pair': her flexibility against building costs in an inflationary fall is the other (aha 9; 3e area 5).

Mon 16 Nov: 3e support for pattern 2: the S&L time mismatch sized (415 insolvent, 32% of assets); textbook in outline.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e no-forced-sale clause: S&L losses were not 'only on paper' because deposits could leave, Laura's are because nothing she owes can be called; competes with SVB (Q3b) for the one clause, never both.
Mon 16 Nov: store; kills 'not a credit failure': the mismatch made the insolvency, credit losses made the bill.
Mon 16 Nov: store; the $153bn bill; row 12 dates the $25bn closing cost to 1982, so say six times the 1982 cost, not 1983.
Mon 16 Nov: store; fraud 10-15% of S&L losses, riding on hidden losses; the RTC count is a search extract.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a or 3e, pattern 2 the safe way round; 0.5-10.5 months, $1,572 and 7.76 against 9.94 years match NUMBERS 1 and 8h; say 'matched payment by payment' beside TNA's duration-matching.
Mon 16 Nov: store, pattern 9; 'counts on no backstop at all' collides with the register's backstop (the extra Treasuries) and with SIPC in row 32: say no outside guarantor or insurer of value.
Mon 16 Nov: store; the cleanest late-not-lost case for savers (RISDIC 1991, paid nearly in full, up to 18 months late).
Mon 16 Nov: 2.3 or 3a clause: a failed insurer's fixed annuity took two years to restart and 16 to settle; adds the timeline to store Q2a-009.
Mon 16 Nov: store; Executive Life sold annuities, structured settlements and GICs through one promiser; links to the 26 U.S.C. 130(d) reserve aha.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; dates verified, recovery unread; serves no part.
Mon 16 Nov: store; a bank deposit is a bank's promise (Cyprus, 47.5% converted); the broker's cash sweep is the one set-up choice to watch.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e or Table 3 custody line: a statement is not ownership, so holdings are checked by CUSIP and published fund holdings.
Mon 16 Nov: store; theft at a keeper costs money and time (72% of allowed claims after 17 years).
Mon 16 Nov: store; Peregrine's forged bank statements; futures customers outside SIPC, so a parallel only.
Mon 16 Nov: store; MF Global paid 100% but took over two years, which corrects store Q2a-022's 'days, not money' for MF Global.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; LBIE from a secondary case summary, judgment unread (S 3).
Mon 16 Nov: 3e custody clause: Rule 15c3-3 is why a broker failure costs fully paid securities time, not money.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e, answers the readers' 'fund sponsors': BlackRock runs the funds but does not hold their Treasuries; custodian bank still unnamed (read IBTM's SAI).
Mon 16 Nov: store; the absence after one search is UNVERIFIED (say 'none found'); 40.7%, 2.4%, 45.6% and $103,178 match NUMBERS 8h and 4.

Mon 16 Nov: store; the 0.5% cut covers only the floor and top: a lending loss in the five payment funds falls on the ten, met at forwards by the extra Treasuries' surplus but not at 0% (NUMBERS 8h: standard met exactly).

Mon 16 Nov: 3e and Table 3 custody row; $589,655 is NUMBERS 8k's all-money total in 1 Jan 2033 money incl. the contribution paid Dec 2032 (about $474,000 after it, store Q30-034), not a broker balance, and one broker is a set-up assumption: needs a NUMBERS entry for the peak balance and its dates.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e clause, the US record's one blemish was a delay (1979; details secondary); drop 'which is why': the rungs pay early by design, so say a delay of days falls inside the 10-47 days each pays early.
Mon 16 Nov: the same bridge as Q2a-021 ($39,225 after $10,775 waiting); adds only the 10-29 days and the seven-day cap, both already in the store (8h, Q36-012).
Mon 16 Nov: 3e pattern 7; figures match NUMBERS 5, but per the AHA register state the missed deposit at 0% ($57,455) and drop '$3,016 at forward rates'.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e pattern 8: Laura herself is the one failure no structure removes ($444,545 matches 8h); its guard is IPS l.17, never 'cannot be raided'.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a one sentence on where losses sat, extending store Q2b-005; always 'read here', a bounded list, never 'every promise that broke'.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e and Table 3; now names the readers' three patterns, the real parties and the missed deposit at 0% truthfully; fix (5)'s $589,655 (not a broker balance, row 32) and add the funds' NAV payout on the five payment rungs (NUMBERS 3; row 31).
Mon 16 Nov: 3e, the parties named; IBTM is one of the five iBond funds (not 'and IBTM'), and the Treasury-bill ETF holding all waiting money (which one UNVERIFIED, NUMBERS 0) is missing.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e naming rule: the Treasury the one promise, the funds, custodian and broker its keepers; consistent with Book 19.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a reserve aha: hibernation defined; Russell's 105-110% trigger is on corporate-bond yields, a weaker yardstick than Laura's.
Mon 16 Nov: store; the lifecycle stages; she skips them because the case fixed the ten, not by skill.

Mon 16 Nov: 3a; funding not age decides hibernation, and 99.5% is labelled Keel arithmetic on NUMBERS 1, but it sits under row 1's 105% trigger: never 'she hibernates' or 'funded at Treasury prices on day one'; say nearly funded, finished January 2028 (IPS l.13).
Mon 16 Nov: 2.0 or 3a citation: lock the fixed promise once funded, only the surplus at risk (IPS l.11); never name his dynamic strategy.
Mon 16 Nov: 2.3 citation for the career argument's timing; the IPS's career argument is l.9 and the pitch, not l.5-6; never Black's tax reason.
Mon 16 Nov: references only; the UK actuarial case for matching, about 25 years before practice.
Mon 16 Nov: store; abstract only, and its tool is a custom liability index, not a ladder.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a precedent a judge can look up: Boots sold all equities for long AAA bonds held passively while still open; it bought agency bonds over gilts, so never 'only government bonds'.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a, Boots's aim reads like the IPS; line refs wrong: the twins are IPS l.11 and l.17 ('A fall in the market is not one of them'), not l.9 and l.21.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a clause: even Boots kept a 5% reinvestment cushion; Laura's extra Treasuries are about 11% ($34,369 of $302,287, labelled Keel arithmetic on NUMBERS 2) and mostly return.
Mon 16 Nov: store; Boots's costs fell from about 0.5% to almost nothing; hindsight on timing.
Mon 16 Nov: store; Boots's choice became the industry's over twenty years; consultant figures.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a context clause on how long pensions took (bonds 28% to 71%, 2006-2025).
Mon 16 Nov: store; 95.8% on buy-out conflicts with TPR's 62% in surplus (row 15): quote each with its date.
Mon 16 Nov: store; the regulator's end-state measure, reached after 2022's yield rise; dated and model-specific.
Mon 16 Nov: a monthly gauge of the same rise row 13 carries over twenty years; October figures from trade press.

Mon 16 Nov: 3a; 'no closer' for 2009-2017 is strong, but 'Laura is there in month one' implies funded on day one: say matched in month one, funded on her own standard in January 2028.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a wording guard for the aha: most pensions end with an insurer, so 'the state a pension reaches last', never 'every pension'.
Mon 16 Nov: store; run-on for surplus has IPS l.11's shape; the surveys' samples differ.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a: UK law's significant-maturity line (10 years; 100% low dependency by the relevant date), the yardstick behind row 22.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a reserve aha; 10.06, 10.02, 10.22 and 9.06 years are Keel arithmetic not in NUMBERS: needs a NUMBERS entry before use, kept apart from NUMBERS 1's 9.94 and TNA's duration-matching.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a contrast for row 22: a typical closed UK scheme was 15-20 years from the line in 2020, average 13 years in 2025.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e honest limit: she counts as mature because her stream is short, not because payments began; the $93,941 waiting (NUMBERS 2) is what the extra Treasuries close.
Mon 16 Nov: 2.0 or 3b: the UK code's objective 'does not apply to any surplus', IPS l.11's rule in law; credit allowed there, Treasuries only here.
Mon 16 Nov: 3b clause: VT 6.6% at cost ($29,829 of $450,000, NUMBERS 8g's 6.63%) sits inside hibernating plans' 0-15% growth slice.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a: Laura's matched block is stricter than a pension's (UK bonds 34.8% corporate, 44.4% index-linked); she can afford Treasuries because the deposit about equals the price.

Mon 16 Nov: 3a or 2.0 clause: the industry calls cash-flow matching LDI's final phase, Laura's first trade; vendor sources.
